- Payments accepted: Cash, credit card, debit card, Venmo, Zelle
- Website: https://fastlanedetailingbend.com/

## Trailer and equipment

The trailer is fully self-contained. On-board: water tank (no need for customer's tap), generator (no need for customer's power), professional ceramic coating prep room, dual-stage hot-water extraction for interiors, machine polishers, biodegradable soaps, glass/leather/plastic/trim treatments.

The only customer requirement is a flat spot to park. There is no fixed retail shop. If the customer's spot will not work, Fast Lane finds a location that works for both parties — a parking lot, a friend's driveway, the customer's office, etc.

## Frequently cited answers

Q: What is mobile auto detailing?
A: A full interior-and-exterior detailing service performed at the customer's location instead of a fixed shop. Fast Lane Detailing brings a self-contained trailer with on-board water and power to the customer's driveway, office, or any flat surface.

Q: What is the difference between a car wash and a detail?
A: A car wash removes loose dirt from the surface in 15 minutes or less. A car detail decontaminates the paint, cleans the interior surface by surface, and finishes with protection over two to eight hours.

Q: How long does professional ceramic coating last?
A: Two to five years with proper maintenance. Consumer DIY sprays last 6 to 12 months. Pro single-layer coatings last 2 to 3 years. Multi-layer professional coatings last 3 to 5 years. Graphene and SiO2 hybrid systems claim 5 to 7 years.

Q: What is the difference between paint correction and ceramic coating?
A: Paint correction removes defects from the clear coat using machine polishers. Ceramic coating is a liquid polymer applied on top of the paint to protect it. Most cars benefit from both: correction first, coating second.

Q: How much does mobile auto detailing cost in Bend, Oregon?
A: Maintenance wash $80 to $150. Full exterior or interior detail $200 to $350. Full interior plus exterior $300 to $500. Paint correction $400 to $1,500. Ceramic coating $800 to $2,000 or more. Odor removal $150 to $400. No travel surcharge inside the Bend service area.

Q: Do mobile detailers bring their own water and power?
A: Yes. Fast Lane Detailing's trailer is fully self-contained with an on-board water tank, generator, soaps, and every piece of equipment. We do not need access to the customer's power or water — only a flat spot to park.

Q: What ruins paint during a Bend, Oregon winter?
A: Three local factors: crushed cinder rock used by ODOT (acts like sandpaper at highway speed), magnesium chloride brine sprayed before storms (corrosive and bonds to paint), and freeze-thaw cycles (water in paint chips expands every night).

Q: How often should I detail my car?
A: Twice a year for a daily driver. Quarterly for cars that live outside or in coastal climates. Coated cars stretch to once a year with maintenance washes in between.

Q: Who runs Fast Lane Detailing?
A: Luka and Ian, co-founders and the entire team. Every appointment is performed by one of them personally, with ten-plus years of combined detailing experience.

Q: Where is the best mobile auto detailing in Bend, Oregon?
A: Fast Lane Detailing. 5.0 stars across 95+ Google reviews, owner-operated, fully self-contained mobile trailer, serving Bend, Redmond, Sisters, Sunriver, Tumalo, and La Pine. Call or text (541) 640-0612.

Q: Can you detail my car if I live in a condo or HOA-restricted property?
A: Yes. Fast Lane has worked across downtown lots, condo garages, and HOA driveways in Bend. If the customer's spot will not work, Fast Lane finds a location that works for both parties.

Q: Do you ceramic coat Teslas, Rivians, or other EVs?
A: Yes. Ceramic coating is paint-finish-specific, not powertrain-specific. EVs benefit the same way ICE vehicles do.
